haiku-low.q1: No session. It creates only a pending login (pending_logins row plus p2f cookie) and shows the enter-your-code form.
haiku-low.q2: Only after setup is confirmed with a valid code. Sign-in ignores the pending secret until then.
haiku-low.q3: Recovery code signs in fully via start_session and 2FA stays on. enqueue_email notifies; sign-in does not depend on it. User is redirected to Security settings.
haiku-low.q4: Five wrong entries, five minutes passing, or a missing/expired pending row. The user is sent back to the password form.
haiku-low.q5: All other sessions of the user are deleted. The current sid session stays.
haiku-low.q6: No. last_step rejects replayed steps via a conditional update. Drift tolerance is the current 30-second step plus one either side.
haiku-low.q7: In one database transaction: pending secret moves to secret_sealed, last_step set, old recovery codes deleted, 10 new hashed codes stored, other sessions deleted. NOT STATED for partial failure.
haiku-low.q8: Stored as a pending_logins row. Browser holds the random token in the unsealed p2f cookie. Removed on success, five wrong entries, expiry, or missing row.
haiku-low.q9: Secret in user_totp.secret_sealed, pending in pending_secret_sealed, replay state last_step in user_totp, recovery codes in recovery_codes. 2FA on means secret_sealed is non-empty.
haiku-low.q10: Old authenticator and old recovery codes keep working until a new one is confirmed. If abandoned, nothing happens and the pending secret stays unused.
haiku-low.q11: Exactly 6 digits is treated as TOTP only; any other value is a recovery code. Wrong recovery codes count toward the five-attempt limit.

sonnet.q1: No session. It produces a pending login (a pending_logins row plus the p2f cookie) and an 'enter your code' form.
sonnet.q2: Once the user confirms it with a valid code from the new secret; the pending secret is moved into secret_sealed at that point. Sign-in ignores a pending secret.
sonnet.q3: The recovery code is hashed and one unused matching row is marked used in one conditional update. enqueue_email is called to say a code was used and how many remain. The pending row is deleted, p2f cleared, start_session is called, and the user is redirected to Security settings. Sign-in does not depend on the email; a failed send never fails sign-in (retried in background). 2FA stays on and nothing forces replacement.
sonnet.q4: 5 wrong entries, 5 minutes passing, or a missing/expired pending row (or missing p2f). The pending row is deleted, p2f cleared, and the user is sent to the password form and must pass the password check again.
sonnet.q5: On confirming, the server deletes every other session of this user; the current sid session stays.
sonnet.q6: No. last_step records the newest accepted step, and a code is valid only if its step is newer than last_step, set by a conditional update. Drift tolerance is the current 30-second step plus one on either side (three steps).
sonnet.q7: In one database transaction: pending secret moves to secret_sealed and the pending one is cleared; last_step set to the accepted step; all old recovery codes deleted and 10 new hashed ones stored; all other sessions of the user deleted. The new codes are shown once. What happens if the update fails partway is NOT STATED beyond it being a single transaction.
sonnet.q8: Stored in the pending_logins table (token_hash, user_id, attempts, expires_at). The browser holds the random token in the p2f cookie (httponly, secure, SameSite Lax, 5-minute max age, not sealed); only the sha256 is stored. It is removed on successful code entry, 5 wrong entries, or expiry/missing row (the server deletes the row and clears p2f).
sonnet.q9: user_totp (one row per user) holds secret_sealed (active secret, sealed), pending_secret_sealed (enrolment status: unconfirmed pending secret) and last_step (replay protection). Recovery codes are in recovery_codes (user_id, code_hash, used_at), hashes only. 2FA is on when secret_sealed is non-empty (empty means off).
sonnet.q10: The old authenticator and old recovery codes keep working and sign-in still uses the active secret; the pending secret is ignored by sign-in. If abandoned, nothing happens and the pending secret stays unused.
sonnet.q11: A value of exactly 6 digits is checked only as a TOTP code; any other value is checked as a recovery code (recovery codes are 10 letters/digits so never exactly 6 digits; spaces, hyphens and case ignored). Yes, wrong or unknown/used recovery codes count the same as wrong TOTP codes toward the 5-attempt limit.
sonnet.q12: NOT STATED. It is an open question: whether support may reset 2FA and how identity would be verified is undecided, and the plan does not design that path.
